To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fourfold model of change agent roles provides a more accurate representation of change agency in organizations than one dimensional models.
the change agent roles are multifaceted and can be classified into four models: leadership, management, consultation and team models.

(1) change agents are often expected to be leaders, managers, and/or consultants, (2) change agents are expected to play different roles, depending on the context of the change, and (3) the four models of change agent roles provide a useful framework for understanding change agent roles in organizational change.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of change agent roles in organizational change.
the nature of agency in change and its implications for the practice and management of organizational change.
the nature of the roles that change agents play in organizational change.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
change agents can be seen as individuals who are able to influence the process of change within organizations.

the role of change agents is to manage and facilitate change, to help organizations and their members adapt and respond to the challenges and opportunities of change, and to ensure that change interventions are effective and successful.
change agents are people who have been given the responsibility of initiating, managing, and implementing changes in an organization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
change agents can be conceptualized as individuals who initiate, manage and implement change in organizations.
we found a lack of consensus among the researchers on the meaning of the concept of change agent.
we have developed an integrative model of change agency that provides a more realistic and balanced picture of change agent roles than existing models.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are four different types of change agents, and each one has a specific role in the process of change.
the roles of change agents are more complex than is often assumed, and that change agency is not a one-dimensional concept, but a multifaceted and multidimensional phenomenon.
the roles change agents perform are not limited to initiating change, but extend into managing and implementing it.
